docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Nutrition tracker documentation Nutrio

Nutrio is a lightweight food tracking app focused on one job: make daily calorie and macro tracking fast enough to use every day. The product combines a React frontend, a small Express API, and PostgreSQL persistence behind a simple mobile-first interface.

For Users For Developers

At a glance

  • Add reusable food products
  • Log meals by section and amount
  • Track calories, protein, fat, and carbs
  • Separate data per browser with a generated deviceId
  • Run locally with Docker or a local PostgreSQL instance

Stack

React 19 TypeScript Vite Express 5 Prisma PostgreSQL Docker Nginx

3 main screens in the app 6 meal sections per day 100 products returned per API call 1000 day entries fetched per overview request

docs.title: What Nutrio covers
docs.text:
Product catalog

Save food items once, including serving size and nutrition values per 100 grams. The app then reuses those products when logging meals.

Daily meal logging

Organize entries into breakfast, snack, lunch, second snack, dinner, and late snack sections without building a full scheduling system.

Nutrition summary

Aggregate daily totals and compare them with built-in targets for calories and macronutrients.

Simple infrastructure

Run the frontend through Nginx, the API through Node.js, and store all persistent data in PostgreSQL using Prisma migrations.

docs.title: Choose your path
docs.text:
For users

Start with User Guide if you want to use Nutrio as an app: create products, log meals, inspect totals, and fix mistakes.

For developers

Start with Developer Guide if you need local setup, architecture, API details, deployment notes, or troubleshooting.

docs.title: Documentation map
docs.text:
User documentation

Includes the app workflow, main screens, daily targets, product creation, meal logging, and privacy expectations.

Developer documentation

Includes setup, Docker and local run modes, architecture, API behavior, deployment topology, and failure recovery.

Current product scope

Nutrio intentionally keeps scope small. There is no account system, no multi-user collaboration, and no external nutrition database integration in the current implementation.

docs.title: POST /day-entries
docs.text: Creates a logged meal entry from a saved product.

docs.title: Request body
docs.text:
{
  "productId": "cm123...",
  "amount": 125,
  "eatenAt": "2026-05-31T08:00:00.000Z",
  "deviceId": "demo-device"
}

docs.title: Validation rules
docs.text:
• productId is required
  • amount must be a non-negative number
  • eatenAt must be a valid date string
  • deviceId is required

docs.title: Success response
docs.text: Returns HTTP 201 and the created dayEntry.

docs.title: Failure responses
docs.text:
• HTTP 400 for invalid request data
  • HTTP 404 if the product does not exist

docs.title: DELETE /day-entries/:id
docs.text: Deletes a stored day entry by its ID.

docs.title: Example request

docs.title: Success response
docs.text: Returns HTTP 204 No Content.

docs.text:
Unexpected failures return HTTP 500 with:

{

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text: Nutrio is intentionally small. The architecture favors a low operational footprint and a short request path over abstraction-heavy layering.

docs.title: System map
docs.text:
Browser UI (React + Vite)
        |
        v
Nginx reverse proxy
        |
        v
Express API
        |
        v
Prisma + PostgreSQL

docs.title: Frontend responsibilities
docs.text:
The frontend is a React 19 application with three primary responsibilities:

  • manage screen navigation between Today, Add, and Products
  • fetch products and nutrition overview data from the API
  • create and delete day entries, then refresh the visible daily summary

Important client-side behaviors:

  • a persistent deviceId is created in localStorage
  • the selected date is grouped locally and rendered through the calendar
  • the frontend sends timezoneOffsetMinutes when loading the nutrition overview

docs.title: Backend responsibilities
docs.text:
The Express API handles:

  • health checks
  • product creation and listing
  • nutrition overview aggregation
  • day entry creation
  • day entry deletion

The backend also contains the nutrition calculation logic:

  • converts product nutrition values from per 100 g into entry totals
  • aggregates totals per day
  • compares totals with built-in daily targets
  • calculates under / ideal / over calorie status

docs.title: Product creation
docs.text:
1. The user submits the Add form.
  2. The frontend sends POST /api/products.
  3. The API validates input and creates the product through Prisma.
  4. The new product becomes available for later meal logging.

docs.title: Daily overview
docs.text:
1. The frontend sends GET /api/nutrition-overview.
  2. The request includes deviceId and timezoneOffsetMinutes.
  3. The API loads matching day entries from PostgreSQL.
  4. The API groups entries into day buckets and computes totals.
  5. The frontend renders the summary card and meal sections.

docs.title: Day entry creation
docs.text:
1. The user picks a product and amount.
  2. The frontend sends POST /api/day-entries.
  3. The API looks up the product, calculates entry nutrition, and stores a new row.
  4. The frontend refreshes the overview.

docs.title: Product
docs.text: Field Type Notes id String Prisma cuid() name String Product name servingSize String Defaults to 100 g calories Float Per 100 g protein Float Per 100 g fat Float Per 100 g carbs Float Per 100 g

docs.title: DayEntry
docs.text: Field Type Notes id String Prisma cuid() name String Copied from the product at entry creation time amount Float Amount in grams calories Float Calculated for the selected amount protein Float Calculated for the selected amount fat Float Calculated for the selected amount carbs Float Calculated for the selected amount deviceId String Browser-scoped identity eatenAt DateTime Timestamp used for day grouping

docs.title: Identity model
docs.text:
No account system

Browser storage is the current identity boundary. If localStorage is cleared or a different browser is used, the app behaves like a different user.

This model is simple and frictionless, but it also means:

  • data portability is limited
  • there is no password recovery or account ownership
  • user separation depends on the browser-generated identifier

docs.title: Container topology
docs.text:
The Docker setup runs four services:

Service Role frontend Builds the Vite app and serves static assets through Nginx api Runs Prisma migrations and starts the Express server db PostgreSQL data store pgadmin Optional database administration UI

docs.title: Deployment
docs.text: This page documents how Nutrio is packaged and what the runtime topology looks like.

docs.title: Docker services
docs.text: Service Image or build Purpose frontend Local Dockerfile Builds the frontend and serves it through Nginx api Local Dockerfile.api Runs Prisma migrations and starts the API db postgres:16-alpine Stores products and day entries pgadmin dpage/pgadmin4:latest Optional inspection UI for the database

docs.title: Published ports
docs.text:
Port Service Use 8080 frontend Main application URL 5050 pgAdmin Database administration

The API stays internal to the Docker network and is reached through Nginx.

docs.title: Frontend container behavior
docs.text:
The frontend image uses a two-stage build:

  1. node:22-alpine installs dependencies and runs npm run build
  2. nginx:1.27-alpine serves the generated dist/ directory

Nginx also proxies /api/* to the API container and serves the SPA with try_files ... /index.html.

docs.title: API container behavior
docs.text:
The API image:

  1. installs dependencies
  2. copies prisma/ and generates the Prisma client
  3. copies the server/ directory
  4. runs npm run prisma:migrate:deploy && npm run api:start

This means schema migrations are applied automatically when the API container starts.

docs.title: Deployment checklist
docs.text:
• Set strong values in .env before publishing the stack
  • Confirm PostgreSQL data volumes are persistent
  • Confirm http://<host>/api/health returns 200
  • Confirm frontend routing works after reloading deep links
  • Confirm the API container can reach the database before accepting traffic

docs.title: Environment hardening notes
docs.text:
The current stack is good for development and small deployments, but consider these upgrades before production use:

  • add authentication if data should be user-owned rather than browser-owned
  • protect or remove pgAdmin in public environments
  • add structured logging and monitoring
  • back up PostgreSQL volumes
  • review entry deletion rules and ownership validation

docs.title: Static documentation publishing
docs.text: The MkDocs site itself is configured separately from the main Nutrio application and can be published to GitHub Pages or any static hosting provider after running a standard MkDocs build in an environment where MkDocs is installed.

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
Nutrio can be started in two ways:

  • Docker Compose for the fastest end-to-end setup
  • Local development if you want to run the frontend and API separately

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text: Tool Why it is needed Node.js 22 Required for local frontend and API execution npm Used for package installation and scripts Docker Required for the containerized workflow PostgreSQL Required only for local API development outside Docker

docs.title: Fastest path: Docker Compose
docs.text:
Recommended for first run

If your goal is to try the app quickly, start with Docker. It gives you the frontend, API, database, and pgAdmin in one command.

docker composedocker-compose 
cp .env.example .env
docker compose up --build

cp .env.example .env
docker-compose up --build

After startup, these endpoints should be available:

Service URL App http://localhost:8080 pgAdmin http://localhost:5050 API health check http://localhost:8080/api/health

docs.title: What the Docker setup does
docs.text:
• Builds the Vite frontend and serves it through nginx:1.27-alpine
  • Starts the API on port 3000 inside the Docker network
  • Starts PostgreSQL 16
  • Runs npm run prisma:migrate:deploy when the API container starts
  • Exposes pgAdmin for database inspection

docs.title: Local development
docs.text: Use this path if you want live frontend development with Vite and direct control of the API process.

docs.title: 1. Install dependencies
docs.text: npm install

docs.title: 2. Provide a PostgreSQL connection
docs.text:
The local API reads DATABASE_URL from the shell environment. It does not load .env automatically, so export the variable before starting the API.

Example:

export DATABASE_URL="postgresql://nutrio:change_me_to_a_strong_password@localhost:5432/nutrio?schema=public"

docs.title: 3. Generate the Prisma client and run migrations
docs.text:
npm run prisma:generate
npm run prisma:migrate:deploy

docs.title: 4. Start the API
docs.text: npm run api:start

docs.title: 5. Start the frontend in another terminal
docs.text:
npm run dev

The Vite frontend runs on http://localhost:5173 and proxies /api requests to http://localhost:3000.

docs.title: Environment variables
docs.text: Variable Used by Purpose POSTGRES_DB Docker Compose Database name for the PostgreSQL container POSTGRES_USER Docker Compose Database user for the PostgreSQL container POSTGRES_PASSWORD Docker Compose Database password for the PostgreSQL container PGADMIN_DEFAULT_EMAIL Docker Compose Login email for pgAdmin PGADMIN_DEFAULT_PASSWORD Docker Compose Login password for pgAdmin DATABASE_URL Local API and Prisma Direct PostgreSQL connection string

docs.title: First-run checklist
docs.text:
• Open the app and confirm the main screens Today, Add, and Products
  • Create one product on the Add screen
  • Log that product into any meal section on the Today screen
  • Confirm GET /api/health returns { "status": "ok" }

docs.title: Useful commands
docs.text:
npm run build
npm run prisma:generate
npm run prisma:migrate:deploy

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: This page focuses on the most likely operational and development issues in the current Nutrio setup.

docs.title: Symptom
docs.text: The API process exits immediately on startup.

docs.title: Cause
docs.text: The local API expects DATABASE_URL to exist in the shell environment.

docs.title: Fix
docs.text:
export DATABASE_URL="postgresql://nutrio:change_me_to_a_strong_password@localhost:5432/nutrio?schema=public"
npm run api:start

docs.title: Symptom
docs.text:
The API is reachable, but the health endpoint reports:

{
  "status": "error"
}

docs.title: Cause
docs.text: The API could not reach PostgreSQL.

docs.title: Fix
docs.text:
• verify the database container or local PostgreSQL instance is running
  • verify credentials in DATABASE_URL
  • inspect API logs for Prisma or connection errors

docs.title: Frontend loads but API calls fail with 502
Symptom
docs.text: The UI opens, but product or overview requests fail behind Nginx.

docs.title: Cause
docs.text: The frontend container is alive, but the API container is down or unhealthy.

docs.title: Fix
docs.text:
• run docker compose ps
  • inspect the API container logs
  • confirm the API health check passes
  • confirm database migrations did not fail during container startup

docs.title: Data appears missing in another browser
Symptom
docs.text: You created products or entries before, but another browser or private window shows an empty state.

docs.title: Cause
docs.text: Nutrio separates data by the browser-generated deviceId.

docs.title: Fix
docs.text:
• use the same browser profile where the data was created
  • avoid clearing localStorage if you want to keep the same local identity
  • move to a real account system if cross-device continuity is required

docs.title: Entries show up on the wrong calendar day
Symptom
docs.text: An entry looks shifted into the previous or next day.

docs.title: Cause
docs.text: The overview is grouped using the browser-provided timezoneOffsetMinutes.

docs.title: Fix
docs.text:
• verify the system timezone on the client device
  • verify the client clock is correct
  • recreate the request and inspect the timezoneOffsetMinutes query value

docs.title: Symptom
docs.text: The API container restarts repeatedly or the local prisma:migrate:deploy command fails.

docs.title: Cause
docs.text: The database may be unavailable, credentials may be wrong, or a previous schema state may conflict with the current migrations.

docs.title: Fix
docs.text:
• verify PostgreSQL connectivity first
  • inspect the exact Prisma error message
  • confirm the target database is the expected one
  • run npm run prisma:generate again if the Prisma client is stale

docs.title: Symptom
docs.text: The app refuses to save a new product.

docs.title: Cause
docs.text: One or more required nutrition fields are empty or invalid.

docs.title: Fix
docs.text:
• provide a non-empty name
  • provide non-negative numeric values for calories, protein, fat, and carbs
  • keep the serving label if you do not need a custom one

docs.title: User Guide
docs.text: This guide follows the normal user workflow inside Nutrio.

docs.title: Main screens
docs.text: Screen Purpose Today Review the selected day, add entries to meal sections, remove mistakes Add Create reusable food products Products Browse and search saved food products

docs.title: 1. Create a product
docs.text:
Before you can log meals, you need at least one saved product.

  1. Open the Add screen.
  2. Enter a product name.
  3. Enter a serving label such as 100 g.
  4. Fill in Kcal, Protein, Fat, and Carbs.
  5. Click Save Product.

Note

Nutrition values are stored as non-negative numbers. The default serving label is 100 g.

docs.title: 2. Log food into a meal section
docs.text:
1. Open the Today screen.
  2. Find the meal section where the entry belongs.
  3. Click +.
  4. Select a saved product.
  5. Enter the amount in grams.
  6. Submit the dialog.

The app creates a day entry, recalculates totals, and refreshes the summary automatically.

docs.title: 3. Review daily progress
docs.text:
The summary card on top of the Today screen shows:

  • consumed calories
  • remaining calories
  • daily progress in percent
  • consumed protein, fat, and carbs
  • target values for the tracked nutrients

Current built-in daily targets:

Metric Target Calories 1600 kcal Protein 120 g Fat 53 g Carbs 160 g

docs.title: 4. Use the calendar and meal groups
docs.text:
Nutrio groups entries by calendar day and shows them in these sections:

  • Breakfast
  • Snack
  • Lunch
  • Second Snack
  • Dinner
  • Third Snack

Use the calendar at the top of the app to switch between days and inspect previous totals.

docs.title: 5. Remove an incorrect entry
docs.text:
1. Open the correct day on the Today screen.
  2. Find the meal card containing the wrong entry.
  3. Click Delete.
  4. Wait for the summary to refresh.

docs.title: 6. Browse products
docs.text:
Open the Products screen to:

  • inspect all saved products
  • search by product name
  • compare nutrition values quickly before logging a meal

docs.title: 7. How data separation works
docs.text:
Nutrio does not use sign-in. Instead, the frontend generates a browser-specific deviceId and stores it in localStorage under the key nutrio:deviceId.

Practical consequences:

  • your data is separated per browser profile
  • clearing browser storage can make old data appear disconnected
  • opening the app in another browser creates a different identity

docs.title: 8. Privacy expectations
docs.text: Nutrio stores food products and day entries in PostgreSQL. Data is not anonymous from an infrastructure perspective, but the current product uses browser-generated identity rather than named user accounts.
